summary: Anthropic describes the lifting of a two-week US government export-control suspension on its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, the safety-classifier fix it deployed, a proposed cross-industry jailbreak severity framework with Amazon, Microsoft and Google, and expanded pre-release testing and information-sharing collaboration with the US government.

mechanisms.reason: The US government applied and then lifted export controls directly on frontier model access based on user nationality, an unprecedented form of AI-specific trade restriction distinct from hardware controls.
mechanisms.quote: On Friday, June 12, the US government applied export controls to our newest models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.

mechanisms.reason: Anthropic claims Mythos 5 exceeds nearly all human experts and other models at finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities, indicating a step-change cyber capability that triggered government concern.
mechanisms.quote: Claude Mythos 5 can be used to find and exploit software vulnerabilities more effectively than any other model—and all but the most skilled human security experts.

categories.reason: Model access via AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry was suspended and is being restored, affecting the cloud platforms that host and distribute these models.
categories.quote: We will re-enable access on AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry as quickly as possible.

notable_reason: This documents the first known case of a US government export control being applied directly to a frontier AI model's access based on user nationality, a novel regulatory precedent with implications for how AI capability and deployment risk is governed going forward.
